mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the federal funds rate over 3 consecutive months signals a shift toward monetary easing, lowering discount rates and increasing the present value of expected equity cash flows, thereby driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% triggers a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and compressing the present value of expected equity cash flows, which produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in tightening periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) above 150,000 jobs signals a strengthening labor market, which increases consumer confidence and corporate investment, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
